evidence.source: 國學大全 字形演變
evidence.text: The page lists 忘 in late Spring and Autumn bronze, Warring States writing, seal script, clerical script, and regular script, including a late Spring and Autumn bronze vessel and named bronze corpora. It describes the graph as 心 semantic plus 亡 phonetic from bronze through regular script. This supports the compound analysis in later early forms; it does not establish that those are the earliest forms, since the page supplies no oracle-bone form.
evidence.title: 忘字形演变字源

evidence.source: 日本語版ウィクショナリー
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 忘 as 形聲, 心 plus phonetic 亡. It gives Mandarin wàng, Middle Chinese mjangH, and Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *maŋ and *maŋ-s. These are distinct reconstructed forms/tones; they support a sound relationship in that analysis, but the entry is tertiary and does not independently establish an ancient sound change or the characters' original senses.
evidence.title: 忘 - ウィクショナリー日本語版

evidence.source: 說文解字 as quoted by 中國哲學書電子化計劃
evidence.text: The entry quotes 許慎: “不識也。从心从亡，亡亦聲。” It records the Han lexicographic gloss “not to recognize/know” and the traditional 心 + 亡 sound-component analysis. Shuowen is a historical account, not by itself confirmation of the graph's earliest formation.
evidence.title: 忘 - 中國哲學書電子化計劃

search_audit.query: 忘 甲骨文 金文 說文 字形 早期 用例; 忘 character oracle bone bronze forms Shuowen earliest attestation; 說文解字 忘 不識也 从心从亡 亡亦聲; 忘 詩經 用例 忘 訓詁 意義; 亡 忘 上古音 Baxter Sagart phonetic component 亡; Baxter Sagart 2014 忘 OC *maŋ-s 亡 MC mjang; 忘 字源 形聲 心 亡 古文字; Unihan 忘 kMandarin Unicode
search_audit.outcome: Ran eight distinct initial queries in one search call. Inspected the Japanese Wiktionary and 國學大全 pages. Search results also surfaced the MOE Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants and CText Shuowen quotation, but the MOE page failed with cache miss and CText returned 403 on open. Official Unihan records were attempted directly and were inaccessible.

gaps: No securely dated oracle-bone occurrence or evidence that 忘 existed in Shang writing was verified. Search results and the inspected paleographic summary support bronze and later forms, but do not establish the earliest attested graph.

The bronze-form listing includes late Spring and Autumn and Warring States examples, but this pass did not inspect glyph images; no visual claim is made about their exact strokes or possible corruption.
The Shuowen wording is preserved as a quotation through a modern web dictionary; the primary MOE character-variant entry could not be opened, so its fuller citations and variants remain unchecked.

No dated early textual occurrence or ordered sequence of semantic extensions (forget, neglect, omit, miss) was established. Shuowen's gloss 不識也 is evidence for a historical lexicographic gloss, not a chronology inferred from modern dictionary senses.

The dossier's Baxter–Sagart local row for 忘 is *maŋ and *maŋ-s (MC mjang and mjangH). The online tertiary entry reports the same forms, but local repository data are not external evidence. No exact local or external Baxter–Sagart row for 亡 was available in this research packet; the phonetic relationship is supported here by the cited lexicographic/paleographic analysis, while same-system character-to-character comparison remains incomplete.

The local Unihan row supplied for 忘 is wàng, but official click-through verification failed. 亡's official current Mandarin record was also inaccessible, and its local exact row was not supplied. Neither current reading is treated as proof of an ancient relationship.

No evidence was located in this bounded pass for competing corruption theories, a separate whole-graph loan, or the dossier's proposed derivation involving a perfective suffix. Those claims remain unresolved rather than accepted or rejected.
